//: layer-shell-cover-screen is upstream's default and is what makes the
//1: open/close animation play correctly. If it ever eats clicks on the
//2: desktop, this is the first thing to set to false.
//3: THE reason swaync is here instead of mako: mako 1.10 has no fade,
//4: animation, transition or opacity option at all, so notifications can
//5: only blink out instantly. transition-time is swaync's notification
//6: animation duration in ms; 0 disables it.
//7: Timeouts carried over from the mako config this replaces, which were
//8: verified by test: normal expires, critical must not. Upstream default
//10: Order is the on-screen order, top to bottom. `notifications` is
//11: placed last deliberately — it is the only widget that grows, so
//12: anything below it would be pushed off a full backlog.

widget-config.//13: Every command here was checked against what is actually installed
widget-config.//14: on this box — pavucontrol, wlogout, swappy and hyprpicker are NOT,
widget-config.//15: so no button calls them. swaync runs these through `sh -c`, which
widget-config.//16: is why $(slurp), the pipe and $HOME all work.
widget-config.//17: The `swaync-client -cp` prefix closes the panel first: the control
widget-config.//18: centre is a layer-shell surface holding keyboard focus, so slurp's
widget-config.//19: region select and swaylock both come up underneath it otherwise.
widget-config.//20: These two sliders do NOT hit the bug that killed waybar's in-bar
widget-config.//21: sliders. That was waybar's ASlider calling set_value() on the very
widget-config.//22: widget under the pointer with no drag interlock (see the WHY THIS
widget-config.//23: EXISTS block in config/sway/sway-quickpanel). swaync drives a plain
widget-config.//24: GtkScale and does not write back mid-drag, so dragging is precise.
widget-config.//25: sway-quickpanel therefore still exists but is no longer the only
widget-config.//26: way to drag these — it stays because it is one keystroke away and
widget-config.//27: does not require opening a full panel.

volume.//: Per-app sliders are off: on this box the list is usually one
volume.//1: entry, and an empty section reads as a rendering fault.

backlight.//: The sysfs device name, confirmed present at /sys/class/backlight.
backlight.//1: A wrong name here does not error — swaync logs 'Could not find
backlight.//2: device' once and the slider is simply dead.

widget-config.//28: Shows apps that have suppressed notifications, with a way to clear
widget-config.//29: them. Nothing on this box registers one today, and swaync hides
widget-config.//30: the widget entirely when the list is empty — so it costs nothing
widget-config.//31: until the day something goes quiet and the reason is not obvious.
